sections: 11. What remains in the module, and why

items.text: **An unreadable `x` or `row` becomes 0 without a problem**
items.statedBy: model element Node attribute x default

items.text: **The property grid says reconnecting is done on the canvas**

hostCode.behaviour: `writtenEnd(relation, end)` reads the id an end is written with from the binding's host attributes `writtenFrom` and `writtenTo`, also when the end names no node, the empty text when the key is absent or empty.
A connect whose two ends are one node is refused as a whole with "A node cannot depend on itself.", as the standalone connect command refused it.
A finding names an element by the id the binding read into `storedId`, empty for an entry without one.

The findings are sorted into two groups, the ids (`missing-id`, `duplicate-id`) and then the dependencies' ends (`dangling-relation`, `self-dependency`), within a group by the declaration's line and then by the order they arose; ids are located at their line and every other finding at its element; `fbl.duplicate-key` is reported first, as a warning at its line.
A row is 60 canvas units high; a node's top is `row × 60`, and a y becomes the nearest row, halves away from zero.
A node sits at its `x` and its row's top; a drag writes the dropped x and the nearest row; a point on empty canvas gives `x` and the nearest row for a new node; a relation is not moved.

In the dark theme the notation's surface, border, text and muted text take the standalone host's dark values (`#1E293B`, `#64748B`, `#F1F5F9`, `#94A3B8`); in the light theme the notation's own values stand.

The route `net.etalii.adp.generic.dependencyCurve` is a horizontal bezier between the facing side anchors while the dependency sits clear to the right of its dependent, and a forward loop from the dependent's right side into the dependency's left side otherwise.
The facing anchors of two boxes, the horizontal bezier between them, and the forward bezier that always leaves rightward and arrives from the left, reaching at least 40 or 0.6 of the span behind.
